rounds.text: Ameya Precision Engineers Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 12.48x against a sector benchmark of 21.4x to 22.02x [E1, E6]. The company exhibits outstanding financial efficiency, delivering a robust ROCE of 25.31% and an ROE of 18.5%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 12.9% and 11.24% [E9, E10]. Profitability growth has been stellar, with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 44% and a TTM profit growth of 15%, backed by an expanding operating margin that reached 22% in September 2026 compared to 13% in the year-ago quarter [E18, E19, E26]. Furthermore, the business is debt-free with borrowings dropping to zero in September 2026, and a disciplined discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 269 against a market price of Rs 176, offering a substantial margin of safety of 34.7% [E32, E38, E39]. Conceded: [E29].

The business exhibits severe disconnects between reported earnings and actual cash generation, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.35x for Mar 2026 where profits are far ahead of cash due to potential receivables or accruals issues [E29]. This is further compounded by a negative free cash flow of Rs -0.06 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31] and an alarming lengthening of debtor days from 91.8 to 115 days [E55]. Top-line growth is also sputtering significantly, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of a mere 2% [E16] and a mediocre 5-year compounded sales growth of 10% [E54]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company stubbornly refuses to return capital to shareholders, maintaining a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E53]. Expectations have dangerously outpaced delivery as recently price growth has exceeded profit growth by 49% [E50], leaving the stock sitting near its highs [E41] with an annualized volatility of 53.3% [E47] and a history of deep drawdowns reaching -48.9% [E46]. Conceded: the company carries zero debt [E32, E52], boasts an impressive ROCE of 25.31% [E10], and operates within a capital goods sector experiencing positive tailwinds [E64].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.35x [E29], free cash flow was Rs -0.06 Cr [E31], debtor days rose to 115 [E55], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, the bear's concern over sputtering top-line growth ignores that compounded profit growth over 3 years has surged by 44% alongside a 15% TTM profit growth [E18, E19], while quarterly operating margin expanded to 22% in Sep 2026 compared to 13% in the year-ago quarter [E26]. The valuation is hardly overextended when looking at sector benchmarks: the P/E sits at 12.48x against a sector benchmark of 22.02x, EV/EBITDA is 7.31x versus a sector benchmark of 12.26x, and ROCE reaches an elite 25.31% against a sector benchmark of 12.9% [E6, E10, E11]. Furthermore, price growth exceeding profit growth is underpinned by stellar operating momentum, including a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 pointing to high-confidence buy signals and net profit growth of 72% YoY [E56, E58]. Finally, the balance sheet risk cited by the bear is neutralized by zero debt at Rs 0.00 Cr in Sep 2026, which is backed by a powerful capital goods sector tailwind score of +0.59 [E33, E64].

Conceded: the company carries zero debt at Rs 0.00 Cr in Sep 2026 [E33] and features a sector tailwind score of +0.59 [E64]. However, the bull's reliance on a 12.48x P/E ratio [E6] ignores the filed statements establishing the actual P/E at 21.4x [E1]. Furthermore, pointing to 3-year profit growth of 44% [E18] masks a severe deceleration in the top-line, where compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has slowed to a meager 2% [E16] and poor 5-year sales growth stands at only 10.2% [E54]. The argument that operating momentum justifies price outpacing profit [E50] collapses under the reality of a poor 0.35x cash conversion rate and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.06 Cr in Mar 2026, directly tied to ballooning debtor days that have increased from 91.8 to 115 days [E29, E31, E55]. Finally, celebrating the lack of debt while ignoring a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] alongside a staggering annualised volatility of 53.3% [E47] underscores that shareholders are absorbing substantial risk without receiving cash returns.
